title: TCC Pattern
description: Learn the Try-Confirm-Cancel pattern for distributed transactions in microservices.

data.text: Try-Confirm-Cancel (TCC) is a distributed transaction pattern that uses reservations and compensations instead of locks. Alibaba and eBay use TCC for high-throughput e-commerce transactions where 2PC would cause unacceptable blocking.

TCC has three phases: Try reserves resources and confirms the transaction can proceed. Confirm commits the transaction. Cancel releases the reservation if any step fails. Unlike 2PC, TCC does not hold locks during the try phase, enabling higher concurrency.

data.title: TCC Components
items: Try: Reserve resources and validate the transaction
Confirm: Commit the reservation (must be idempotent)
Cancel: Release the reservation (must be idempotent)
Transaction coordinator: Manages the TCC flow
Reservation TTL: Resources are held for a limited time

data.title: Idempotency is Critical
data.text: Confirm and Cancel operations must be idempotent because network failures may cause retries. If Confirm is called twice, the second call should be a no-op.

data.title: Example: TCC for Hotel Booking
data.code:
# Try Phase
POST /bookings/try
{
  "hotelId": "hotel-123",
  "roomType": "deluxe",
  "checkIn": "2024-06-01",
  "checkOut": "2024-06-05"
}

# Response: Reservation created with 15-minute TTL
{
  "reservationId": "res-789",
  "status": "reserved",
  "expiresAt": "2024-01-15T10:45:00Z"
}

# Confirm Phase (if all steps succeed)
POST /bookings/res-789/confirm

# Cancel Phase (if any step fails)
POST /bookings/res-789/cancel

data.caption: TCC transaction flow
data.definition:
graph LR
    C[Coordinator] -->|1. Try| R[Reserve Resources]
    R -->|2. Confirm| S[Services Confirm]
    R -->|3. Cancel| X[Services Cancel]
    S -->|Commit| DB[(Database)]
    X -->|Release| DB

items.question: How does TCC compare to 2PC?
items.answer: TCC does not hold locks during the try phase, enabling higher concurrency. 2PC holds locks during the prepare phase, blocking other transactions.

items.question: What happens if the TTL expires?
items.answer: The reservation is automatically released. The coordinator should retry or cancel the transaction. Design your TTL based on the maximum expected transaction duration.

items.question: Is TCC widely adopted?
items.answer: TCC is popular in high-throughput e-commerce and financial systems. It requires more implementation effort than Saga but provides better performance for certain use cases.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: TCC uses reservations instead of locks
Confirm and Cancel must be idempotent
Better performance than 2PC for high-throughput systems
data.takeaway: TCC is a powerful alternative to 2PC for high-throughput distributed transactions.
